author: Susan Bloom
title: Monmouth's MultiSports Kingdom is where your sports love never has to fade - NewsBreak
text:
By Susan Bloom ,
19 hours ago MANALAPAN -- Growing up in Holmdel to a family with deep roots in local sports organizations and facilities, Mike Klatsky loved and played several sports throughout his school years.
And after a successful career on Wall Street, he came back to that sweet spot in 2009 by joining other family members and investors in launching what has become MultiSports Kingdom , a network of indoor sports complexes in Manalapan, Marlboro and Monroe that offer everything from basketball, tennis and soccer facilities to football, lacrosse, volleyball and more, taking pride in helping more people experience the joy of sports.
“I played basketball and tennis at Holmdel High School as well as in college,” said Klatsky, 48, a Marlboro resident who vividly remembers running an under-the-radar NCAA gambling pool in high school. “It actually got pretty big with 200 to 300 people, including teachers and administrators, and I ended up getting in trouble with the school,” he laughed. “But I don’t mind talking about it, because I know I won’t get detention for it now!”
A love of sports ran in the family.

“Nearly 40 years ago, my father Fred started the Mid-Monmouth Basketball League, a travel basketball league for all of Monmouth and Ocean County, and in 1990 my family bought Jersey 34 Tennis Club in Matawan, which my mother Kathy still runs,” Klatsky said.
“About 10 years ago, my cousin Brian Klatsky (co-owner of Under the Glass pinball lounge in Red Bank ) started Team Rio, a high-level Amateur Athletic Union (AAU) basketball team, along with his own training company and facility," Klatsky continued. "My brother Dave is an assistant coach for the University of Florida men’s basketball team, my sister’s husband is the head coach of the men’s basketball team at Columbia University in New York City, and my wife Marie played basketball at Marist College in Poughkeepsie, New York, and is undoubtedly the best athlete among us.”
The bottom line? “Sports are in our family’s blood,” Klatsky said.
After graduating from the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School with a business degree after high school, “I worked as a fixed income salesman at three different investment banking firms on Wall Street and enjoyed a great career and experience in finance,” Klatsky said.
But after a decade in the finance world, a unique opportunity that combined Klatsky’s business and management skills with his love of sports proved too good for him to pass up.

“In 2005, my dad put together an investor group with me included to build a new 80,000-square-foot sports facility in Monroe that would have basketball and tennis, two sports where we had deep ties,” he explained. “It took four years to get it going, but we finally opened that first site in 2009 with five tennis courts, two basketball courts and a turf field.
"I was still working on Wall Street at the time, but over the next couple of years I found myself doing a lot of scheduling work for the new facility from my desk, and by 2011, I felt that if I could commit to it, we could really make something out of that business,” said Klatsky, who finally left Wall Street in 2012 to join the new venture full-time.
With their following for team and league games in multiple sports growing beyond their space in Monroe, Klatsky and his fellow owners expanded their business by adding a 15,000-square-foot facility in Marlboro in April 2021 and a 170,000-square-foot facility in Manalapan in October 2024 and bringing all of those separate facilities together under a new brand called MultiSports Kingdom.
Shore prep sports top prospects for: 117 girls soccer players for 2026
A million strong “Today, we run skill sessions, training, camps and team and league play and most of our customers come to our facilities for a scheduled game or practice, though we also set aside some time for open play and pickup games,” said Klatsky, who believes that more than a million people come through the doors of their three facilities in any given year.
“We originally started out with just a few basketball leagues and teams when we first opened and have since grown to host over 2,000 basketball teams per year across four seasons, and it keeps growing,” Klatsky said. “While we offer basketball in Marlboro and Manalapan (and Marlboro is a basketball-only facility), our Manalapan location specializes in turf activities like soccer, baseball, softball, lacrosse, football and kickball, and Monroe specializes in tennis, pickleball and the racket sport padel.”
Staffed by roughly 25 employees and 50 to 70 part-time coaches, tennis pros, desk staff and others, “we focus on all-level athletes as opposed to elite teams; we want beginners, intermediate players, and everybody — that’s a key to our success,” Klatsky said. “The benefit of playing sports isn’t about winning, but about the teamwork and camaraderie that sports promote. Going through the trenches with somebody regardless of the result is a bond that you can’t replicate anywhere else, and you can experience that on your middle school junior varsity team,” he said. “That’s what we try to promote at all levels.”
According to Klatsky, MultiSports Kingdom facilities cater largely to residents of all ages who live within a 30-minute drive of their locations. “But on weekends, when we run tournaments, we can also see players traveling to us regionally from places like New York, Pennsylvania and other East Coast locations,” he said.

General pricing for their space ranges from about $20 to $30 per hour for programs/teams, which Klatsky said translates to a cost of roughly $200 to $300 per season per player.
Among trends in the sports facility market, “pickleball remains super-hot, though more facilities have opened to serve that demand, and tennis and basketball are still as strong as ever,” Klatsky said. “Youth sports in general have exploded to near-obsessive levels, with young athletes training more and spending more money on it and the whole category getting more exposure than ever. Women’s sports are more popular than ever too,” said Klatsky, who noted that three of their own MultiSports Kingdom investment partners — basketball legend Sue Bird, soccer World Cup champion Megan Rapinoe and Grand Slam tennis champion Kim Clijsters — are among the top women in their fields.
As the youth sports category continues to grow by leaps and bounds, Klatsky said that one of MultiSports Kingdom’s challenges involves dealing with parents’ expectations and intensity.
“After a league game, half of the people go home upset because they lost and many parents blame the refs or complain that their child didn’t play enough,” he said. “We work hard to help parents maintain perspective, balance their expectations, and deal with the outcomes of games and their children’s goals in a positive and productive way.”

A fun, competitive environment Looking ahead, “we hope to keep expanding geographically and continue growing our brand,” Klatsky said. “Our newest facility, the former Hoop Group in Neptune, will join the MultiSports Kingdom family this October, and it hopefully won’t be our last addition.”
Among their favorite parts of the job, Klatsky and MSK CEO Margie Blank take pride in helping to develop the organization’s staff.
“We offer great employment opportunities for college students and post-college individuals and are a fun, young, sporty environment to be in,” he said. “We also have some staff members who are at the tail end of their career, such as retired teachers and law enforcement professionals, and it’s a great opportunity for them too. Our full-time staffers — some of whom have been with us since the beginning — have all been extremely loyal and we appreciate them and couldn’t achieve any of our success without them.”
As for himself, a self-described “big math guy” who enjoys a good sports battle, “the scheduling I do for MSK locations is complicated and I love what we’ve put together for our leagues and teams, and I also love all of the players, coaches, owners and other great people we get to meet through this business,” Klatsky said.
“The experience we offer at MultiSports Kingdom is unlike anything else,” Klatsky confirmed. “Everyone here is so friendly and it’s a fun, competitive environment where people can engage in their favorite sports, embrace and respect the competition and enjoy a great game.”

MultiSports Kingdom Locations: Manalapan (150 Woodward Road), Marlboro (2 Timber Lane), and Monroe (4 Farrington Boulevard)
Opened: 2009
Owners: Mike Klatsky and others
Website: www.multisportskingdom.com
